---
title: "Clustering samples on factors"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
                      fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 96, message = FALSE,
                      warning = FALSE)
```

Factor models compress many features into a few factors; clustering on those
factors is often more robust than clustering on the raw features, because noise
and view size imbalance are reduced.

```{r}
library(factomics)
sim <- simulate_multiomics(n_samples = 60, n_groups = 3, seed = 1)
res <- run_factor_pipeline(sim$data,
                           methods = c("PCA", "MFA", "FABIA", "GFA", "JIVE"),
                           k = 4, verbose = FALSE)
truth <- setNames(sim$metadata$group, sim$metadata$sample)
```

## One matrix

`cluster_samples()` clusters any samples x features matrix with k-means,
hierarchical clustering (Ward) or PAM. Give several values of `k` and the one
with the highest mean silhouette width is kept:

```{r}
cl_mfa <- cluster_samples(res$MFA$scores, method = "hclust", k = 2:6)
cl_mfa
cl_mfa$by_k
```

By default the factor scores are **not** re-standardised, so each factor keeps
its own variance and weak or noise factors weigh less. Use `scale = TRUE` to
give every factor equal weight.

## Every method at once

```{r}
cl <- cluster_results(res, cluster_method = "kmeans", k = 2:6)
cl
```

```{r, fig.height = 4}
plot_clusters(cl, "silhouette")
```

## Agreement between methods and with known labels

```{r}
cmp <- compare_clusterings(cl, truth = truth)
round(cmp$agreement, 2)
cmp$vs_truth
```

```{r, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 5.5}
plot_clusters(cl, "agreement", truth = truth)
```

## Clusters in an embedding

Pass the clustering to `plot_embedding()` to colour each method's embedding by
its own clusters:

```{r, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 10}
emb <- embed_results(res, type = "umap")
plot_embedding(emb, clusters = cl, shape_by = "group",
               metadata = sim$metadata)
```

## Comparing algorithms

```{r}
algos <- c("kmeans", "hclust", "pam")
ari <- sapply(algos, function(a) {
  cl_a <- cluster_results(res, cluster_method = a, k = 2:6)
  setNames(compare_clusterings(cl_a, truth)$vs_truth$ARI,
           cl_a$summary$method)
})
round(ari, 2)
```
